chunks.arabic_text: وَسُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: عَنْ صَلَاةِ النَّافِلَةِ بِالنَّهَارِ فِي سَفَرٍ

translations.en: Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام was asked about the nafilah prayer during the daytime while traveling.

chunks.arabic_text: فَقَالَ: «لَوْ صَلَحَتِ النَّافِلَةُ فِي السَّفَرِ تَمَّتِ الْفَرِيضَةُ»

translations.en: So he said: "If the nafilah were valid in travel, the obligatory prayer would have been complete."

en.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of daytime nafilah prayers during travel. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام indicates that since the obligatory prayer is shortened in travel, the daytime nafilah tied to the full resident prayer is not maintained.
en.seo_question: Can daytime nafilah prayers be performed while traveling in Shia Islam?

key_terms.صَلَاةِ: prayer; the ritual salat being discussed
key_terms.النَّافِلَةِ: supererogatory prayer; a non-obligatory devotional salat
key_terms.بِالنَّهَارِ: during the daytime; specifying the time of the nafilah in question
key_terms.سَفَرٍ: travel; the legal state affecting prayer rulings
key_terms.صَلَحَتِ: were valid or appropriate; indicating legal suitability
key_terms.الْفَرِيضَةُ: the obligatory prayer; the prescribed salat whose form changes in travel
